column4: This ayah itself joins the section's whole movement: God يُخْرِجُ ٱلْخَبْءَ, brings the hidden thing out, and knows what people conceal and disclose.
The exact sound pair appears: whether speech is made loud, God knows the secret and what is still more hidden.
God's knowing ٱلْجَهْرَ مِنَ ٱلْقَوْلِ and what people conceal is a direct restatement of the section's voiced/inward pair.
Secret speech and loud speech are equal before God; the same ayah extends the pair into one who hides by night and moves openly by day.
Whether people keep their speech secret or voice it openly, God knows what is within breasts, precisely joining tongue and interior.
People fold their breasts and cover themselves with garments to hide, yet God knows what they conceal and disclose; literal covering and inward secrecy meet.
The concise pair يَعْلَمُ سِرَّكُمْ وَجَهْرَكُمْ directly matches God's knowledge of the secret and the open.
God couples knowledge of the unseen heavens and earth with knowledge of what creatures reveal and conceal.
The ayah asks whether they do not know that God knows both what they keep secret and what they publish.
What is inside the self remains known and accountable whether it is disclosed or hidden, closely matching speech on the tongue or in the heart.
Nothing in earth or heaven is hidden from God, stating the knowledge claim behind the section without limiting it to speech.
What breasts hide or reveal is known by God; the concealed interior and its outward disclosure are explicitly paired.
Hostility has appeared from mouths while breasts hide still more, making speech the audible edge of a deeper concealed state.
God tests what is in breasts, purifies what is in hearts, and knows the breasts' contents, turning the covered interior into something brought to proof.
Good may be shown or hidden; the ayah keeps moral action valid in the same two states that the section gives to remembrance and recitation.
The messenger's task of conveying is set beside God's knowledge of what people disclose and conceal, linking delivered speech to complete knowledge.
The prayer states that God knows what people hide and declare and that nothing on earth or in heaven is hidden from Him.
God knows what people conceal and what they make public, an exact nonlexical parallel to the section's pair.
The ayah repeats that God knows what people conceal and declare in the context of hidden pride.
At the boundary between inhabited and uninhabited houses, God knows what people show and conceal; spatial privacy and inward privacy coincide.
God knows what breasts keep enclosed and what people announce, directly opposing the inner container to public expression.
Whether anything is displayed or hidden, God knows it; the wording exactly enacts the section's two conditions.
The Prophet is consoled over people's saying because God knows both what they keep secret and what they proclaim.
God knows the furtive betrayal of eyes and what breasts conceal, extending hiddenness from inward speech to a nearly imperceptible glance.
Those who distort God's signs cannot hide from Him, giving the divine-knowledge claim a concrete adversarial setting.
God hears both their secret and their private consultation, explicitly placing concealed speech within divine hearing.
Every private conversation, however few or many its speakers, is attended by God's knowledge; secrecy changes no part of its audibility to Him.
A secretly conveyed affection is answered by God's knowledge of what was hidden and what was announced, making covert communication the test case.
God knows what people conceal and disclose and what breasts contain, uniting outer act and inner state.
God knows the hypocrites' secret and private counsel, a direct case of speech kept below public hearing.
God knows what the self whispers within, supplying the inward pole of the section's tongue-and-heart reading.
No word is uttered without a ready watcher; with the inward whisper of 50:16, this supplies the outward pole of the same speech pair.
God brings out what the disputants were concealing about the killing, an exact human instance of the hidden being extracted.
The messenger makes clear much of the Scripture that people had hidden, so revelation itself draws covered speech into the open.
They enter with unbelief, leave with it, and God best knows what they concealed; outward passage fails to expose the inward state to people but not to God.
What people formerly hid becomes manifest to them, directly realizing the section's contrary dictionary sense of خفي as disclosure.
The hypocrites fear a surah will report what is in their hearts, and God promises to bring out what they fear disclosed.
The Prophet conceals something within himself that God will disclose, an explicit movement from inward cover to manifestation.
Those with disease in their hearts suppose God will not bring their rancor out; the ayah names the extraction of a concealed interior.
A secretly entrusted statement is passed on and God discloses it to the Prophet, joining quiet speech, concealment, and divine disclosure.
On the day of presentation, no hidden thing among people remains hidden, the eschatological completion of the section's movement.
The day when inner secrets are tested makes what was covered in persons answer publicly.
What is stored in breasts is brought out and gathered, a concrete extraction of the inwardly concealed.
All people are fully exposed on the day when nothing about them is hidden from God.
The earth casts out what is inside it and becomes empty, staging concealed contents emerging from their covering.
The earth brings out its burdens, a literal and eschatological realization of أخرج from under cover.
Even a mustard seed hidden in a rock, heaven, or earth is brought by God, combining minute concealment, knowledge, and retrieval.
God knows the unseen and even a grain in the darknesses of earth, giving the section's hidden seed beneath soil its exact epistemic depth.
Fruit emerging from its sheaths and every conception and birth occur within God's knowledge; covering, خروج, womb, and knowing converge.
God knows what every female carries and every increase or decrease in wombs, making the covered womb a measured hidden place.
God brings people out of their mothers' wombs while they know nothing, opposing divine extraction and knowledge to human unawareness.
One ayah joins what is settled in wombs and brought out as children with rain that stirs dead earth and makes growth appear.
Knowledge of the Hour, rain, and what is in wombs belongs to God, gathering three concealed things the section treats as known or brought forth.
No female conceives or gives birth except with God's knowledge, pairing the hidden interior with its eventual issue.
Human formation occurs creation after creation within three darknesses, a precise concrete image of life covered from sight.
God knew people when they were embryos concealed within their mothers, directly joining womb-hiddenness and prior knowledge.
Joseph is placed in the غَيَابَتِ ٱلْجُبِّ, the hidden depth of a well, giving the section's well image a literal act of concealment.
A bucket draws Joseph from the well into view, yet the travelers hide him as merchandise while God knows what they do.
A treasure lies covered beneath a wall until the children are to extract it, a timed movement from protection and concealment to خروج.
The raven scratches earth to show how to cover a body, presenting earth as the material boundary between exposed and hidden.
Satan whispers in order to expose what had been concealed from the pair of their bodies, explicitly linking secret speech to unveiling.
Their covered bodies become visible and they immediately patch leaves over themselves, enacting exposure followed by renewed covering.
Their bodies become visible and they begin covering themselves with garden leaves, a second direct scene of the hidden made manifest.
The ban on striking feet lest hidden adornment become known shows an unseen object disclosed through sound.
God declares the Hour coming while describing it as almost kept hidden; concealment here belongs to the future moment only He knows.
Denial of the Hour is answered by the Knower of the unseen, from whom not even an atom is hidden in heaven or earth.
God is Knower of the unseen and does not expose His unseen to anyone, stating the rule of concealment.
The exception is a chosen messenger, before whom God discloses guarded knowledge; it completes the boundary stated in 72:26.
God alone knows the unseen duration, and the ayah joins that knowledge with unsurpassed seeing and hearing.
Reciting any portion of the Quran occurs under God's witness, and no atom is hidden from Him; recitation and exhaustive awareness meet in one ayah.
The Prophet is told not to move his tongue hastily with revelation, fixing the section's outward, bodily pole of recitation.
God assumes responsibility for gathering the revelation and its recitation, the inner retention needed before voiced reading.
When God recites it, the Prophet is to follow its recitation, completing the tongue-and-retention sequence of 75:16-17.
The Prophet did not previously recite a book or copy one with his hand, sharply distinguishing received recitation from reading a prior text.
The signs are clear within the breasts of those given knowledge, supplying the inwardly held counterpart to 29:48's recitation.
The Quran's measured recital is said to steady the Prophet's heart, directly linking voiced revelation with inward fixing.
When the Quran is recited, God places a concealed veil between the Prophet and deniers; audible reading produces an unseen covering.
Coverings on hearts and heaviness in ears prevent understanding the recitation of 17:45, joining inward cover and blocked hearing.
The command to remember the Lord upon forgetting directly connects remembrance with the boundary of retained recitation.
Hearts become tranquil through God's remembrance, explicitly locating dhikr in the inward organ named by the section.
At the fire God commands Moses to establish prayer for His remembrance, joining divine speech, dhikr, and prayer as in the section's 87:15 link.
Moses sees a fire and approaches for a brand or guidance; it is the visible threshold to the hidden speaker of 20:11 and the concealed Hour of 20:15.
On reaching the visible fire, Moses is called by name, making heard address emerge from the scene whose speaker was not first visible.
Moses sees a fire from afar and expects either news or a burning brand, the same visible approach to divine address.
When Moses reaches the fire, a call comes to him from the blessed fire-side; visible flame and heard but unseen address meet.
The caller identifies Himself as God, completing the voice-from-fire scene of 27:7-8.
Moses sees a fire from the side of the mount and goes seeking news or an ember, repeating the approach from a visible sign to a voice.
The call comes from the valley's bank, from the tree in the blessed ground, giving the hidden voice a precisely described spatial cover.
The hoopoe brings Solomon sure news of something beyond Solomon's present knowledge, enacting concealed reality becoming report.
The hoopoe sees a people prostrate to the sun while Satan blocks the way; conspicuous light becomes the occasion of spiritual covering before 27:25 names the One who reveals hidden things.
God does not love evil made public in speech except by one wronged, giving جهر its concrete vocal and ethical limit.
Believers are forbidden to raise their voices above the Prophet's or speak loudly to him as to one another, an exact calibration of voiced speech.
Those who lower their voices with the Messenger are praised, supplying the restrained counterpart to 49:2's prohibited loudness.
On that day voices are humbled for the Merciful until only a whisper is heard, reversing ordinary public speech into near-silence.
Zechariah calls his Lord with a hidden or quiet call, a direct Qur'anic instance of prayer kept low.
People call God humbly and secretly amid danger on land and sea, locating quiet supplication in a concrete crisis.
The command to call the Lord humbly and secretly directly sets the sound and inward posture of prayer.
The command places remembrance within oneself, humbly and fearfully, below loud speech, exactly joining heart and measured voice.
Noah's hearers put fingers in ears and wrap themselves in garments, using bodily covering to block a proclaimed voice.
Noah says he called his people openly, supplying one vocal mode after the resistance described in 71:7.
Noah combines public proclamation with private, secret appeal, placing both modes of one message side by side.
The garden owners proceed while whispering to one another, a narrative instance of deliberately lowered speech concealing intent.
The wrongdoers keep their private consultation secret, providing a concrete hidden-speech scene immediately before God's knowledge is asserted.
God knows every saying in heaven and earth and is the Hearer, completing the secret consultation of 21:3.
Pharaoh's magicians dispute their plan and conceal their private counsel, another explicit case of speech withdrawn from public hearing.
God knows an inward intention that will be mentioned, while the ayah regulates secret promises and the proper spoken word.
A covert promise is made to those who hate revelation, and God knows their secrets; hidden speech stands within His awareness.
Alms may be made visible or hidden; the latter state is explicitly named and valued, showing one act across openness and cover.
Secret and public spending are paired with the exact word جَهْرًا, extending open/hidden duality beyond speech.
Rain descends and God brings forth the growth of every thing, including palm clusters, staging life emerging from covered earth.
Heavy cloud is driven to dead land, rain falls, and fruits are brought out; the ayah explicitly compares this with bringing out the dead.
Good land brings out its vegetation by its Lord's permission, making earth the cover from which growth appears.
Water descends from the sky and varied pairs of plants are brought forth, the closest parallel to pasture extracted by rain.
People eat and pasture their cattle from the plants of 20:53, identifying the emergence specifically as provision and grazing.
Water is driven to barren ground and crops are brought out for livestock and people to eat, closely matching the pasture scene.
Dead earth is revived and grain is brought out from it for eating, joining concealment underground with visible provision.
Rain is channeled as springs through earth, then crops are brought out before fading, tracing hidden water into manifest growth.
Measured rain revives dead land and the ayah says people will similarly be brought out, uniting vegetation and resurrection.
Human beings are described as made to grow from earth like plants, fusing the pasture emergence with human origin.
God returns people to earth and will bring them out again, completing 71:17's plant-human analogy.
Water is poured abundantly, the first action in the emergence sequence completed by 80:26-31.
Earth is split open, making an aperture for the growth named in the following ayat.
Grain is caused to grow from the split, watered earth, the edible instance of what was concealed below.
Fruit and pasture emerge in the same sequence, explicitly naming the object of 87:4's image.
The returning-rain sky supplies the first half of a compact rain-and-opening image.
The earth is characterized by splitting open, completing 86:11 and matching emergence from a covering.
Healing drink comes out from within bees, a concrete non-soil instance of something beneficial emerging from a covered interior.
Stones split and water comes out, providing a material instance of hidden water becoming visible.
Water is sent in measure and lodged in earth, describing the concealed phase before springs and growth become visible.
If water sinks beyond reach, only God can bring flowing water, a precise boundary between covered water and water visible at hand.
At the trumpet blast people rush out from graves, making the grave a cover from which human life emerges.
Earth splits away from people as they emerge quickly, a direct resurrection form of the section's خروج image.
People come out of graves like scattered locusts, closely echoing creatures emerging through openings in earth.
People come out of graves at speed toward the summons, another explicit passage from covered earth into public assembly.
Prayer must be neither made loud nor reduced to inaudibility; the commanded middle path sets the boundary between the section's two sound poles.
Israel's demand to see God جَهْرَةً ends in the thunderbolt, showing that open visibility can exceed the eye rather than grant knowledge.
The demand to see God openly is answered by the thunderbolt, repeating the limit of visual disclosure.
Lightning nearly takes sight; its flashes reveal a path only intermittently before darkness stops movement, making excessive light and obscurity alternate.
The flash of lightning nearly removes sight, directly supporting the section's claim that too much light can function as a veil.
Moses asks to see God, but the manifestation crushes the mountain and leaves him unconscious; disclosure itself overwhelms perception.
Eyes do not encompass God while He encompasses all vision, marking a strict boundary between creaturely seeing and divine awareness.
Layered darkness makes a person's own hand nearly invisible; lack of light supplies the opposite visual covering to blinding brightness.
Water may sink so deeply that its owner cannot seek it, reversing the section's cleaned well whose water has become visible.
God does not expose believers indiscriminately to the unseen but chooses messengers, defining who may receive what was hidden.
Punishment arriving openly rather than suddenly uses جَهْرَةً for manifest arrival, an important non-vocal sense of the section's root.
The condemned look with a stealthy, concealed glance; خَفِيٍّ shifts hiddenness from speech to the eye's manner.
Luqman commands moderation in walking and lowering the voice, another explicit measure placed on audible speech.
People confronted with an opened heavenly sight claim their eyes have been dazzled, a plausible instance of visibility defeating reliable vision.
The eye is dazzled at the onset of the last day, giving the section's visually overwhelmed eye an eschatological form.
Only God reveals the Hour at its time and it arrives suddenly, a direct parallel to the Hour kept hidden in 20:15.
Questioners about the Hour are told its knowledge is only with God, reinforcing the concealed time of 20:15.
Final knowledge of the Hour rests with the Lord, another boundary around what remains hidden from human speakers.
No one in the heavens and earth knows the unseen except God, stating the epistemic boundary behind the hoopoe's claim.
No hidden thing in heaven or earth lies outside a clear record, extending 27:25's ٱلْخَبْءَ beyond what the bird has observed.
God is the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, a compact conceptual equivalent of hidden and open.
Return to the Knower of unseen and witnessed will result in people's deeds being reported back to them, moving hidden action into disclosure.
After human work is seen, all return to the Knower of unseen and witnessed who reports what was done.
God is Knower of unseen and witnessed; it supplies the governing category immediately before 13:10 applies it to secret and loud speech.
The Knower of unseen and witnessed is exalted above false partners, grounding comprehensive knowledge in divine uniqueness.
The Creator described in the surrounding passage is Knower of unseen and witnessed, joining hidden knowledge to ordering creation.
The prayer invokes the Knower of unseen and witnessed to judge disclosed disagreement.
God alone is named Knower of unseen and witnessed, the abstract pair corresponding to the section's concrete open and hidden states.
After death overtakes those fleeing it, they return to the Knower of unseen and witnessed who discloses their deeds.
Knower of unseen and witnessed follows the explicit secret/public knowledge of 64:4 and summarizes its range.
Giving by night and day, secretly and publicly, shows one righteous act persisting through hidden and manifest conditions.
Spending secretly and publicly appears alongside patience, prayer, and repelling evil, extending the two-state pattern to worshipful action.
Believers are commanded to pray and spend secretly and publicly before the day when ordinary exchange ends.
Those who recite God's Book, pray, and spend secretly and publicly bring recitation and the two modes of action into one ayah.
The command to remember the Lord's name and devote oneself to Him echoes 87:15, while the section supplies its inward and voiced modes.
The command to read one's own written record provides the visible-text pole against the section's recitation from the heart.
The Quran is divided so the Prophet may recite it to people deliberately, presenting revelation as paced, outwardly heard speech.
The Prophet is told not to hurry the Quran before its revelation is completed, paralleling the controlled tongue and retention of 75:16-18.
The trustworthy Spirit brings the revelation down, beginning the movement completed by 26:194-195 from source to heart to Arabic speech.
Revelation descends upon the Prophet's heart, the interior location from which warning will be voiced.
The revelation is in a clear Arabic tongue, completing 26:194's passage from heart to articulate language.
The first command is to recite in the Lord's name, giving the section's act of reading its imperative form.
God teaches by the pen, providing a written, visible vehicle beside the oral recitation commanded in 96:1.
Pure milk is given from within cattle, from between waste and blood, an extraction of a clean, visible provision from a concealed interior.
A drop is placed in a secure resting place, identifying the womb-like enclosure before emergence.
Successive hidden transformations culminate in another creation, completing the enclosed process begun in 23:13.
The human drop is placed in a secure enclosure, another concrete covered interior.
It remains there until a known measure, making the hidden interval both bounded and divinely measured.
Rain revives earth after death and disperses creatures across it, a nonlexical parallel to hidden life becoming perceptible.
Rain mingles with earth's vegetation until it becomes full growth, staging the rapid passage from water and soil to visible provision.
God sends rain and brings forth fruits as provision, repeating the causal form of pasture brought out from earth.
Water descends for drink and for vegetation in which livestock graze, beginning a direct pasture scene.
By that water God causes crops, olives, palms, grapes, and fruits to grow, completing 16:10's rain-to-provision movement.
Water revives earth after its death, making previously imperceptible life evident without using the خروج root.
Gardens of palms and grapes are produced by the stored water of 23:18, making underground provision visible and edible.
Rain produces flourishing gardens whose trees people could not grow unaided, another emergence of visible life by divine action.
God brings living from dead and dead from living, revives earth, and says people will likewise be brought out.
Rain from the sky revives earth after death, presenting emergence as a sign perceptible after hidden fear and hope.
Rain is followed by fruits brought out in varied colors, a direct agricultural use of أخرج.
Humbled earth stirs and swells when rain falls; the One who revives it will revive the dead.
Provision descends from heaven and revives earth after death, another concise rain-to-manifest-life relation.
Blessed water descends and begins the garden-and-grain sequence continued in 50:10-11.
Tall palms with layered clusters show ordered growth rising from the rain-fed earth.
The growth feeds servants and revives a dead land, after which human خروج is explicitly compared to it.
Rain-produced growth impresses its cultivators before yellowing and breaking down, preserving the visible phase of what earth brought forth.
Pouring water descends from rain clouds, opening the emergence sequence of 78:15-16.
Grain and vegetation are brought out by that water, the direct counterpart to rain-released pasture.
Dense gardens complete the visible abundance produced in 78:14-15.
Solomon's death remains hidden from the jinn until a ground creature weakens his staff and his fall discloses it, exposing their lack of unseen knowledge.
At judgment there appears to wrongdoers from God what they had never reckoned with, a broader form of concealed reality becoming manifest.
The evil consequences of deeds become manifest and surround those who mocked them, turning formerly unseen outcome into public reality.
The section's dictionary image of under-feathers gives a plausible anatomical underside to birds spreading and folding their wings here, though the ayah itself does not name hidden feathers.
God knows what enters earth and what comes out of it, as well as what descends and ascends, directly pairing a covered location with emergence under divine knowledge.
God knows everything entering earth and emerging from it and remains with people wherever they are, a close formulation of hidden contents and خروج.
God splits grain and date-stone and brings living from dead and dead from living, giving the hidden seed a divinely opened and extracted life.
Rain descends and fruits are brought out as provision, an early direct parallel to pasture brought forth from earth.
Water from heaven makes earth become green, a compact nonlexical version of rain turning covered potential into visible growth.
The hearers are directed to earth and the many noble pairs caused to grow in it, focusing attention on what soil makes visible.
Rain is followed by every noble pair grown in earth, another direct rain-to-emergence scene.
The question directs human sight to the seed they sow, isolating the concealed beginning of cultivated growth.
God asks whether humans make the seed grow or He does, completing 56:63's passage from burial in soil to visible crop.
God brings water and pasture out of earth, naming both the خروج motion and the exact object of 87:4.
Grapes and fresh herbage continue the produce emerging from the split earth of 80:26-27.
Olives and palms add the trees, including the section's palm object, produced by the same opened earth.
Dense gardens complete the sequence between grain in 80:27 and fruit and pasture in 80:31.
A tree comes forth from Mount Sinai bearing oil and food, a concrete plant emerging with useful provision.
Gardens are placed in the revived ground and springs are made to burst there, continuing 36:33 from emerging grain to visible water.
The struck stone releases twelve springs, a direct instance of covered water brought into view.
Moses strikes the stone and twelve springs gush out, repeating the extraction of hidden water for each people.
Earth is burst into springs until its water meets the descending floodwater, forcefully uncovering water from below.
God best knows what is within people's selves, directly covering the inward state that may never reach the tongue.
God is Knower of the unseen in heavens and earth and knows what breasts contain, joining cosmic hiddenness to the human interior.
People say obedience publicly and then plan at night words unlike what they said, while God records the concealed revision.
They hide from people but not from God while holding night counsel about displeasing speech, an exact private-speech test of divine knowledge.
Joseph conceals his response within himself and does not disclose it to his brothers, sharply separating inward speech from utterance.
The Quran is said to be sent by the One who knows the secret in heavens and earth, joining recited revelation to knowledge of the concealed.
No self knows what delight has been hidden for it, giving خفي a concrete sense of a provision kept under divine cover until disclosure.
At judgment people cannot conceal any statement from God, marking the end of speech that could once be privately withheld.
An unseen narrative is revealed to the Prophet despite his and his people's prior ignorance, showing hidden knowledge becoming recited report.
Joseph's story is explicitly called unseen news revealed to the Prophet, another passage from concealed event to spoken revelation.
Zechariah's sign is inability to speak to people except by gesture, yet he is commanded to remember and glorify God much; inward worship persists when ordinary voice is blocked.
Zechariah's sign is that, though sound, he cannot speak to people for three nights, making the presence and absence of voiced expression explicit.
Unable to address them normally, Zechariah signals his people to glorify morning and evening, completing the silent-remembrance scene of 19:10.
God has heard the woman arguing her case and the dialogue she holds with the Prophet, making even a personal conversation fully audible to Him.
Moses asks that the knot in his tongue be loosened, bringing the section's interest in articulation down to the organ of speech.
Moses seeks clear understanding of his speech, giving the communicative purpose of the loosened tongue in 20:27.
The command to recite the Quran in measured fashion gives revealed speech an explicit vocal discipline.
Joseph is placed in the well's hidden depth while God privately reveals that he will later tell his brothers of this deed when they do not recognize him.
God shapes people within wombs however He wills, locating unseen formation inside a physical covering.
Human creation passes through concealed stages before God brings people out as children, explicitly moving womb formation into public life.
A kindled fire lights the surroundings and then God removes the light, leaving the people in darkness unable to see; visibility turns into its opposite.
Darkness, thunder, and lightning surround people who plug their ears against the blast, supplying both obscured sight and deliberately blocked sound before 2:20.
Even if a gate in heaven were opened for people to ascend through, the disclosure would lead to the dazzled-eye claim of 15:15.
God chooses Moses and commands him to listen to revelation, explicitly identifying hearing as the response to the call at the fire.
Solomon cannot see the hoopoe and asks whether it is absent, opening the bird's episode with a problem of visibility before its hidden news arrives.
The hearers describe coverings over their hearts, deafness in their ears, and a barrier between themselves and the Prophet, joining blocked inward reception with blocked sound.
People listen to the Prophet while coverings over hearts and heaviness in ears prevent comprehension, a direct reversal of effective recitation.
Those reminded of God's signs turn away while coverings remain over hearts and heaviness over ears, again making reminder inaudible through inward cover.
Barriers before and behind people are joined by a covering over them so they cannot see, a spatial image of concealed vision.
A person's public speech impresses and he invokes God regarding his heart, yet his conduct reveals fierce hostility, warning that polished utterance may cover its inward opposite.
Once the speaker of 2:204 turns away, he corrupts land and destroys crop and offspring, exposing what the impressive speech had concealed.
The command to abandon both outward and inward sin treats manifest and concealed action as equally real moral domains.
Forbidden indecencies are named in both their outward and inward forms, another ethical boundary spanning visible and concealed states.
God is named the Manifest and the Hidden while knowing all things, placing the section's paired categories at the level of divine names.
Deaf, mute, and blind, the people left in darkness by 2:17 cannot return, showing loss of voice and perception together.
Sunlight turns away from the cave while the sleepers remain within its opening, so measured light protects what God keeps concealed there.
A people at the sunrise have no covering against the sun, supplying the opposite limit to both sheltering cover and light that overwhelms vision.
A revived person given light to walk among people is opposed to one trapped in darkness, presenting light as disclosure and guidance rather than a veil.
The lamp in glass multiplies clear light and God guides to His light, a positive illuminating counterpart to the section's excessive light that blinds.
Earth is spread and prepared before 79:31 states that its water and pasture are brought out.
Earth is extended and every beautiful pair is caused to grow in it, another direct contemplation of life appearing from soil.
The Prophet's wives are told not to soften speech provocatively and to speak appropriately, regulating vocal quality rather than mere loudness.
People call the Prophet from behind private chambers, combining a spatial covering with the poorly measured address corrected by 49:2-3.
The Prophet says he does not know whether the promised event is near or assigned a long term, preparing the unseen-knowledge boundary of 72:26-27.
The unseen of heavens and earth belongs to God and the Hour can arrive in the blink of an eye, connecting its concealed time with sudden disclosure.
People extract ornaments from the sea to wear, extending خروج to a useful object removed from a hidden depth.
From the two bodies of water people eat and extract ornaments, repeating the retrieval of something concealed below the surface.
Pearls and coral come forth from the waters, a compact physical instance of hidden objects emerging.
